page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It features advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 34.85 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.13 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 4403.68 and the bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 30.06 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 32.55 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 20.39 GB/sec, resulting in a weak PassMark memory score of 1586.87.

Despite memory bandwidth constraints, the instance maintains average performance in database operations, static web serving at 8.93 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 6.0 million operations per second. It also handles small-to-medium language model inference at average speeds, processing 35.08 tokens per second for a 7B model prompt. Given its low RAM-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute allocation, the c4n-highcpu-4 offers a resource-dense configuration for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, and basic vector-accelerated mathematical workloads.
